answer_1.quote: Dialogue summarization is a crucial task that aims to extract essential information from a dialogue
models: MoE-based approach with RoR and FG

answer_2.quote: In evaluation, we use both automatic and human evaluations. Following existing studies, the automatic evaluation includes ROUGE (i.e., the F-scores R-1 R-2 R-L) and BLEU (Papineni et al., 2002) that measures the n-gram overlap between the model output and reference summaries, as well as BERT-Score (Zhang et al., 2019c) and Mover-Score (Zhao et al., 2019) that computes the text similarity based on BERT embeddings (Devlin et al., 2019).

answer_4.quote: We perform human evaluation on different baselines and our approaches following the evaluation criteria specified in Section 3.2. Human evaluation metrics include informativeness that measures the coverage of the key points, non-redundancy that evaluates whether the generated summary contains redundant or repeated information, and fluency that examines whether the generated summary is fluent and grammatically correct.
